q: भारत की मानक मध्याह्न रेखा (82°30' पूर्वी देशांतर) भारत के कितने राज्यों से होकर गुजरती है?
e:
Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on 82°30'E longitude, which passes through 5 states: Uttar Pradesh (Mirzapur/Naini near Prayagraj), Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh.
हिंदी: भारत की मानक समय रेखा 82°30' पूर्वी देशांतर 5 राज्यों — उत्तर प्रदेश, मध्य प्रदेश, छत्तीसगढ़, ओडिशा और आंध्र प्रदेश से होकर गुजरती है।
Exam Boosters: (1) IST is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT+5:30). (2) Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N) passes through 8 Indian states (Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram). (3) The Tropic of Cancer and IST intersect in Koriya/Surajpur district of Chhattisgarh. (4) India's longitudinal extent is 68°7'E (Guhar Moti, Gujarat) to 97°25'E (Kibithu, Arunachal Pradesh).
qe: Through how many Indian states does the Standard Meridian of India (82°30'E longitude) pass?

q: भारत के साथ सबसे लंबी अंतर्राष्ट्रीय स्थलीय सीमा किस देश की लगती है?
e:
Bangladesh shares the longest international land boundary with India (4,096.7 km), touching 5 Indian states: West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
हिंदी: बांग्लादेश भारत के साथ सबसे लंबी अंतर्राष्ट्रीय स्थलीय सीमा (4,096.7 किमी) साझा करता है, जो 5 भारतीय राज्यों को स्पर्श करती है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Decreasing order of land borders: Bangladesh (4,096.7 km) > China (3,488 km) > Pakistan (3,323 km) > Nepal (1,751 km) > Myanmar (1,643 km) > Bhutan (699 km) > Afghanistan (106 km). (2) Total land frontier of India is 15,200 km and coastline (including islands) is 7,516.6 km. (3) Tripura is surrounded by Bangladesh on three sides (Zero Line). (4) Radcliffe Line separates India from Pakistan and Bangladesh; McMahon Line separates India from China in the eastern sector.
qe: Which country shares the longest international land border with India?

q: कौन-सा जल चैनल अंडमान द्वीप समूह को निकोबार द्वीप समूह से अलग करता है?
e:
The Ten Degree Channel (along 10°N latitude) separates Little Andaman (in the Andaman group) from Car Nicobar (in the Nicobar group).
हिंदी: दस डिग्री चैनल (10° उत्तरी अक्षांश) लघु अंडमान को कार निकोबार से अलग करता है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy (India) from Maldives. (2) Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the rest of Lakshadweep. (3) Duncan Passage lies between South Andaman and Little Andaman. (4) Indira Point (Great Nicobar) is the southernmost point of India (6°45'N), while Barren Island is India's only active volcano.
qe: Which water channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands?

q:
निम्नलिखित हिमालयी पर्वत श्रेणियों को उत्तर से दक्षिण के सही क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
1. पीर पंजाल  2. काराकोरम  3. ज़ास्कर  4. लद्दाख
e:
Moving from North to South across the Trans-Himalayas and Lesser Himalayas: Karakoram (2) → Ladakh (4) → Zaskar (3) → Pir Panjal (1).
हिंदी: उत्तर से दक्षिण का सही क्रम काराकोरम (2) → लद्दाख (4) → ज़ास्कर (3) → पीर पंजाल (1) है।
Exam Boosters: (1) K2 / Godwin-Austen (8,611 m) is the highest peak in the Karakoram Range and India's highest peak. (2) The Indus River flows between the Ladakh and Zaskar ranges. (3) Kashmir Valley lies between the Greater Himalaya (Himadri) and the Pir Panjal Range. (4) Siachen Glacier (world's highest battlefield) is situated in the eastern Karakoram Range.
qe:
Arrange the following Himalayan mountain ranges in correct order from North to South:
1. Pir Panjal  2. Karakoram  3. Zaskar  4. Ladakh

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा पर्वतीय दर्रा अपने राज्य/केंद्र शासित प्रदेश से सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
e:
Bomdi La Pass is located in Arunachal Pradesh (connecting Arunachal Pradesh with Lhasa, Tibet), NOT Manipur. Tuzu Pass is in Manipur.
हिंदी: बोमडिला दर्रा अरुणाचल प्रदेश में स्थित है, न कि मणिपुर में। मणिपुर में तुजु दर्रा स्थित है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Nathu La and Jelep La are important passes in Sikkim. (2) Shipki La (Himachal Pradesh) is the entry point of the Sutlej River into India; Rohtang and Baralacha La are also in HP. (3) Mana, Niti, and Lipulekh are major passes of Uttarakhand (Lipulekh is used for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra). (4) Zoji La connects Srinagar to Leh; Banihal Pass houses the Jawahar Tunnel.
qe: Which of the following mountain passes is NOT correctly matched with its State/Union Territory?

q: भारत के उत्तर के विशाल मैदान का कौन-सा भाग हिमालय की गिरिपाद में कंकड़-पत्थरों की संकरी सरंध्र पट्टी है जहाँ नदियाँ भूमिगत होकर लुप्त हो जाती हैं?
e:
Bhabar is an 8–16 km wide belt of coarse pebbles and boulders deposited at the foot of the Shiwaliks; due to high porosity, small streams disappear beneath it.
हिंदी: भाबर शिवालिक के गिरिपाद में 8–16 किमी चौड़ी कंकड़-पत्थरों की पट्टी है, जहाँ अत्यधिक पारगम्यता के कारण छोटी नदियाँ विलुप्त हो जाती हैं।
Exam Boosters: (1) Terai lies immediately south of Bhabar, where underground streams re-emerge creating marshy, forested land. (2) Bhangar consists of older alluvium with calcareous nodules called 'Kankar'. (3) Khadar consists of newer, highly fertile alluvium renewed annually by floods. (4) Karewas (lacustrine deposits in Kashmir Valley) are famous for Saffron (Zafran) cultivation.
qe: Which region of the Great Northern Plains of India is a narrow, porous belt of pebbles along the Himalayan foothills where rivers disappear underground?

q:
सूची-I (पर्वत चोटियाँ) को सूची-II (पर्वत श्रेणियाँ) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
सूची-I: (a) गुरु शिखर  (b) धूपगढ़  (c) महेंद्रगिरि  (d) डोड्डाबेट्टा
सूची-II: 1. सतपुड़ा  2. अरावली  3. नीलगिरि  4. पूर्वी घाट
e:
Guru Shikhar (1,722 m, Mount Abu) is the highest peak of Aravalli (2); Dhupgarh (1,350 m, Panchmarhi) is the highest peak of Satpura (1); Mahendragiri (Odisha) is a prominent peak of Eastern Ghats (4); Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest peak of Nilgiris (3).
हिंदी: गुरु शिखर (अरावली), धूपगढ़ (सतपुड़ा), महेंद्रगिरि (पूर्वी घाट) तथा डोड्डाबेट्टा (नीलगिरि) सही सुमेलित हैं। कूट: a-2, b-1, c-4, d-3।
Exam Boosters: (1) Jindhagada Peak (1,690 m, Andhra Pradesh) is technically the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats, though Mahendragiri (1,501 m) is widely cited in NCERT. (2) Anamudi (2,695 m, Kerala) is the highest peak of Western Ghats and South India. (3) Saramati (Nagaland) is the highest peak of Naga Hills; Nokrek is highest in Garo Hills. (4) Aravalli is one of the oldest residual fold mountain ranges in the world.
qe:
Match List-I (Mountain Peaks) with List-II (Mountain Ranges) and choose the correct code:
List-I: (a) Guru Shikhar  (b) Dhupgarh  (c) Mahendragiri  (d) Doddabetta
List-II: 1. Satpura  2. Aravalli  3. Nilgiri  4. Eastern Ghats

q: कृष्णा नदी के डेल्टा और कन्याकुमारी के मध्य स्थित भारत के पूर्वी तटीय मैदान के भाग को क्या कहा जाता है?
e:
The Coromandel Coast extends along Tamil Nadu and southern Andhra Pradesh (from Krishna/Pulicat region to Kanyakumari), receiving winter rainfall from the retreating (Northeast) monsoon.
हिंदी: कृष्णा डेल्टा से कन्याकुमारी तक का पूर्वी तटीय भाग कोरोमंडल तट कहलाता है, जहाँ शीतकाल में उत्तर-पूर्वी मानसून से वर्षा होती है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Northern Circars lies between the Mahanadi and Krishna deltas (Odisha & northern AP); Utkal Plain is specifically the Odisha coast. (2) Western Coastal Plain subdivisions (North to South): Kathiawar/Kachchh → Konkan (Maharashtra–Goa) → Kanara/Kannada (Karnataka) → Malabar (Kerala). (3) Malabar Coast is famous for backwaters (Kayals) like Vembanad and Ashtamudi lakes. (4) Western Coastal Plain is narrower and forms estuaries, whereas Eastern Coastal Plain is wider and forms fertile deltas.
qe: The stretch of the Eastern Coastal Plain of India lying between the Krishna River delta and Kanyakumari is known as:

q:
भारत के प्रायद्वीपीय पठार के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: मेघालय (कार्बी-आंगलोंग) पठार प्रायद्वीपीय खंड का उत्तर-पूर्वी विस्तार है जो मालदा भ्रंश द्वारा अलग होता है।
कथन II: दक्कन ट्रैप का निर्माण क्रेटेशियस काल के अंत में दरारी बेसाल्टिक ज्वालामुखी उद्भेदन से हुआ था।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: कथन I और कथन II दोनों
न तो कथन I और न ही कथन II
e:
Both statements are correct. The Malda Gap (Garo-Rajmahal Gap) separates the Chota Nagpur Plateau from the Meghalaya Plateau (Garo, Khasi, Jaintia hills). The Deccan Trap consists of horizontally layered basaltic lava flows from late Cretaceous fissure eruptions.
हिंदी: दोनों कथन सत्य हैं। मालदा भ्रंश (गारो-राजमहल गैप) छोटानागपुर पठार को मेघालय पठार से अलग करता है, और दक्कन ट्रैप का निर्माण बेसाल्ट लावा प्रवाह से हुआ।
Exam Boosters: (1) Chota Nagpur Plateau is called the 'Ruhr of India' due to rich coal and iron deposits; Parasnath is its highest peak. (2) Malwa Plateau is drained by Chambal, Betwa, and Ken rivers and is known for Chambal ravines (badland topography). (3) Weathering of Deccan Trap basalt produces Black Cotton Soil (Regur). (4) Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia hills are arranged West to East in Meghalaya.
qe:
Consider the following statements about the Peninsular Plateau of India:
Statement I: The Meghalaya (Karbi-Anglong) Plateau is a north-eastern structural extension of the Peninsular Block separated by the Malda Fault.
Statement II: The Deccan Trap was formed by fissure-type basaltic volcanic eruptions during the late Cretaceous period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II

q:
पश्चिमी घाट के निम्नलिखित दर्रों (घाटों) को उत्तर से दक्षिण के सही क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
1. पालघाट  2. थालघाट  3. शेनकोट्टा दर्रा  4. भोरघाट
e:
From North to South along the Western Ghats: Thalghat (Mumbai–Nashik, Maharashtra) → Bhorghat (Mumbai–Pune, Maharashtra) → Palghat/Palakkad Gap (between Nilgiri and Anaimalai hills, Kerala–TN) → Shencottah Gap (Cardamom hills, Kollam–Madurai).
हिंदी: उत्तर से दक्षिण का क्रम: थालघाट (मुंबई-नासिक) → भोरघाट (मुंबई-पुणे) → पालघाट (नीलगिरि व अन्नामलाई के बीच) → शेनकोट्टा दर्रा (इलायची पहाड़ियाँ)।
Exam Boosters: (1) Western Ghats are known as Sahyadri in Maharashtra and Karnataka. (2) Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of India's 4 Biodiversity Hotspots (others: Himalayas, Indo-Burma, Sundaland). (3) Kalsubai (1,646 m) is the highest peak of Maharashtra in the Sahyadris. (4) Cardamom Hills (Elamalai) are the southernmost hill range of India.
qe:
Arrange the following Western Ghats passes (Ghats) in correct order from North to South:
1. Palghat  2. Thalghat  3. Shencottah Gap  4. Bhorghat

q: सर सिडनी बुरार्ड द्वारा किए गए हिमालय के प्रादेशिक विभाजन के संबंध में कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
o: पंजाब हिमालय सिंधु और सतलुज नदियों के बीच स्थित है
कुमाऊँ हिमालय सतलुज और काली नदियों के बीच स्थित है
नेपाल हिमालय काली और तीस्ता नदियों के बीच स्थित है
असम हिमालय तीस्ता और लोहित नदियों के बीच स्थित है
e:
Assam Himalaya lies between the Teesta and Dihang (Brahmaputra) rivers, NOT Teesta and Lohit. All other three regional divisions are accurately matched.
हिंदी: असम हिमालय तीस्ता और दिहांग (ब्रह्मपुत्र) नदियों के बीच स्थित है, न कि तीस्ता और लोहित के बीच। अन्य तीनों कथन सत्य हैं।
Exam Boosters: (1) Nepal Himalaya is the longest regional section (~800 km) and contains Mount Everest, Kanchenjunga, Makalu, and Dhaulagiri. (2) Kumaon Himalaya is the shortest (~320 km) and includes Nanda Devi, Kamet, and Badrinath. (3) Structurally, the three parallel longitudinal divisions are Himadri (Greater), Himachal (Lesser), and Shiwalik (Outer). (4) Syntaxial bends occur at Nanga Parbat (west) and Namcha Barwa (east).
qe: Which of the following statements regarding the Himalayan regional divisions (by Sir Sidney Burrard) is NOT correct?
oe: Punjab Himalaya lies between Indus and Sutlej rivers
Kumaon Himalaya lies between Sutlej and Kali rivers
Nepal Himalaya lies between Kali and Teesta rivers
Assam Himalaya lies between Teesta and Lohit rivers

q: उत्तराखंड के किस संगम (प्रयाग) पर भागीरथी और अलकनंदा नदियाँ मिलकर गंगा का निर्माण करती हैं?
e:
Bhagirathi (originating at Gangotri/Gomukh) and Alaknanda (originating at Satopanth Glacier) merge at Devprayag to take the name 'Ganga'.
हिंदी: देवप्रयाग में भागीरथी और अलकनंदा नदियों का संगम होता है, जहाँ से यह संयुक्त धारा 'गंगा' कहलाती है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Panch Prayag (North to South along Alaknanda): Vishnuprayag (Alaknanda + Dhauliganga) → Nandaprayag (+ Nandakini) → Karnaprayag (+ Pindar) → Rudraprayag (+ Mandakini) → Devprayag (+ Bhagirathi). (2) Ganga enters the plains at Haridwar and has a total length of 2,525 km. (3) Yamuna is the longest tributary of Ganga (meets at Prayagraj). (4) Son is the major right-bank tributary joining Ganga directly from the Peninsular plateau (near Patna).
qe: At which confluence (Prayag) in Uttarakhand do the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers meet to form the Ganga?

q: किस प्रायद्वीपीय नदी को 'दक्षिण गंगा' कहा जाता है तथा जिसका अपवाह बेसिन प्रायद्वीपीय भारत में सबसे बड़ा है?
e:
The Godavari (1,465 km) originates from Trimbakeshwar (Nashik, Maharashtra), has the largest drainage basin in Peninsular India, and is called 'Dakshin Ganga' or 'Vridha Ganga'.
हिंदी: गोदावरी (1,465 किमी) त्र्यंबकेश्वर (नासिक, महाराष्ट्र) से निकलती है और प्रायद्वीपीय भारत की सबसे लंबी व सबसे बड़े बेसिन वाली नदी होने के कारण 'दक्षिण गंगा' कहलाती है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Major tributaries of Godavari: Penganga, Wainganga, Wardha (together Pranhita), Indravati, Sabari, and Manjira (right bank). (2) Kaveri is often called 'Ganga of South India' (sacredness/perennial flow), originating at Talakaveri (Brahmagiri Hills, Karnataka). (3) Krishna originates near Mahabaleshwar; tributaries include Bhima, Tungabhadra, Koyna, Musi. (4) Mahanadi originates in Sihawa (Chhattisgarh) and has the Hirakud Dam (Odisha).
qe: Which Peninsular river is known as 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South) and has the largest river basin in Peninsular India?

q: भारत की सबसे बड़ी खारे पानी की लैगून झील कौन-सी है?
e:
Chilika Lake in Odisha (south of Mahanadi delta) is India's largest brackish-water lagoon and was India's first wetland designated under the Ramsar Convention (1981, along with Keoladeo).
हिंदी: ओडिशा में स्थित चिल्का झील भारत की सबसे बड़ी खारे पानी की लैगून झील है और यह भारत के प्रथम रामसर स्थलों में से एक है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Wular Lake (Jammu & Kashmir, fed by Jhelum) is India's largest freshwater lake. (2) Sambhar Lake (Rajasthan) is India's largest inland salt lake. (3) Loktak Lake (Manipur) is the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India and houses Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park. (4) Pulicat Lake lies on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border (Sriharikota barrier island separates it from Bay of Bengal).
qe: Which is the largest brackish-water lagoon in India?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी गंगा नदी की बाएँ तट (left-bank) की सहायक नदी नहीं है?
e:
Son originates from the Amarkantak Plateau (MP) and flows northward to join the Ganga on its RIGHT bank near Patna. Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Ramganga, Kosi, and Mahananda are left-bank tributaries.
हिंदी: सोन नदी अमरकंटक पठार से निकलकर पटना के निकट गंगा के दाएँ तट (right bank) पर मिलती है। गोमती, घाघरा व गंडक बाएँ तट की सहायक नदियाँ हैं।
Exam Boosters: (1) Left-bank tributaries of Ganga (West to East): Ramganga → Gomti → Ghaghara → Gandak → Kosi → Mahananda. (2) Right-bank tributaries of Ganga: Yamuna, Tamsa (Tons), Son, Punpun. (3) Gomti is the only Himalayan-plain tributary of Ganga that originates from plains (Gomat Taal / Fulhar Lake, Pilibhit, UP). (4) Kosi is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to frequent course shifting.
qe: Which of the following is NOT a left-bank tributary of the Ganga River?

q:
सूची-I (बहुउद्देशीय नदी घाटी परियोजनाएँ) को सूची-II (नदियाँ) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
सूची-I: (a) टिहरी बाँध  (b) हीराकुड बाँध  (c) नागार्जुन सागर  (d) सरदार सरोवर
सूची-II: 1. कृष्णा  2. नर्मदा  3. भागीरथी  4. महानदी
e:
Tehri Dam (Uttarakhand, India's tallest dam, 260.5 m) is on Bhagirathi (3); Hirakud Dam (Odisha, longest earthen dam) is on Mahanadi (4); Nagarjuna Sagar (Telangana–AP) is on Krishna (1); Sardar Sarovar (Gujarat) is on Narmada (2).
हिंदी: टिहरी (भागीरथी), हीराकुड (महानदी), नागार्जुन सागर (कृष्णा) तथा सरदार सरोवर (नर्मदा) सही सुमेलित हैं। कूट: a-3, b-4, c-1, d-2।
Exam Boosters: (1) Bhakra-Nangal Dam (Sutlej, HP–Punjab) creates Gobind Sagar reservoir. (2) Rihand Dam (Gobind Ballabh Pant Sagar) is on Rihand river (Sonbhadra, UP). (3) Idukki Dam (Kerala) is an arch dam on the Periyar River. (4) Mettur Dam (Tamil Nadu) is built on the Kaveri River.
qe:
Match List-I (Multipurpose River Projects) with List-II (Rivers):
List-I: (a) Tehri Dam  (b) Hirakud Dam  (c) Nagarjuna Sagar  (d) Sardar Sarovar
List-II: 1. Krishna  2. Narmada  3. Bhagirathi  4. Mahanadi

q: कर्नाटक में स्थित भारत का सबसे ऊँचा जलप्रपात (455 मीटर) कौन-सा है जो वाराही नदी पर बनता है?
e:
Kunchikal Falls (455 m, tiered waterfall) in Shimoga district, Karnataka, on the Varahi River is the highest waterfall in India.
हिंदी: कर्नाटक के शिमोगा जिले में वाराही नदी पर स्थित कुंचिकल जलप्रपात (455 मीटर) भारत का सबसे ऊँचा जलप्रपात है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Jog / Gersoppa Falls (253 m, Sharavathi River, Karnataka) is India's highest untiered/plunge waterfall in the Western Ghats; Nohkalikai Falls (340 m, Meghalaya) is the tallest plunge waterfall overall. (2) Dudhsagar Falls is on the Mandovi River (Goa–Karnataka border). (3) Dhuandhar Falls (Jabalpur, MP) is formed by the Narmada River over marble rocks. (4) Chitrakote Falls (Indravati River, Chhattisgarh) is called the 'Niagara of India'.
qe: Which waterfall in Karnataka is the highest waterfall in India (455 m) and is formed by the Varahi River?

q: सिंधु जल संधि (1960) के अंतर्गत भारत को किन तीन 'पूर्वी नदियों' के जल का पूर्ण उपयोग करने का अधिकार दिया गया था?
e:
Under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty (brokered by the World Bank), India got full control over the three Eastern Rivers — Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej — while Pakistan got primary rights over the Western Rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab).
हिंदी: विश्व बैंक की मध्यस्थता से 1960 में हुई सिंधु जल संधि के तहत भारत को रावी, ब्यास और सतलुज (पूर्वी नदियाँ) का अधिकार मिला।
Exam Boosters: (1) Chenab is the largest tributary of the Indus, formed by Chandra and Bhaga streams at Tandi (HP). (2) Beas is the only Indus tributary that flows entirely within India (meets Sutlej at Harike Barrage, Punjab). (3) Indira Gandhi Canal originates from Harike Barrage. (4) Tulbul/Wular project is on Jhelum; Salal, Baglihar, and Dulhasti are on Chenab.
qe: Under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), India was allocated unrestricted use of the waters of which three 'Eastern Rivers'?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी नदियाँ मध्य प्रदेश के अमरकंटक पठार से उद्गमित होती हैं?
e:
Both the Narmada (flowing west into the Arabian Sea) and the Son (flowing north-east to join the Ganga) originate from the Amarkantak Plateau (Maikal Range, MP), forming a classic radial drainage pattern.
हिंदी: नर्मदा और सोन दोनों नदियाँ मध्य प्रदेश के अमरकंटक पठार (मैकाल श्रेणी) से निकलती हैं और अरीय अपवाह प्रतिरूप बनाती हैं।
Exam Boosters: (1) Tapti originates from Multai (Betul district, Satpura Range, MP) and flows parallel to Narmada into the Gulf of Khambhat. (2) Chambal originates from Janapav Hills (Vindhyas, near Mhow, MP). (3) Mahi River is the only river in India that crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice. (4) Luni is an ephemeral inland drainage river of Rajasthan that disappears in the Rann of Kachchh.
qe: Which of the following rivers originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh?

q:
ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: तिब्बत में ब्रह्मपुत्र को यारलुंग सांगपो कहा जाता है और यह अरुणाचल प्रदेश में दिहांग/सियांग के रूप में भारत में प्रवेश करती है।
कथन II: विश्व का सबसे बड़ा आबाद नदी द्वीप 'माजुली' असम में ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी द्वारा निर्मित है।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: कथन I और कथन II दोनों
न तो कथन I और न ही कथन II
e:
Both statements are correct. Originating from the Chemayungdung Glacier near Mansarovar (Tibet), Yarlung Tsangpo takes a hairpin bend at Namcha Barwa, enters Arunachal Pradesh as Siang/Dihang, becomes Brahmaputra in Assam (forming Majuli Island), and enters Bangladesh as Jamuna.
हिंदी: दोनों कथन सत्य हैं। तिब्बत में सांगपो कहलाने वाली यह नदी अरुणाचल में दिहांग, असम में ब्रह्मपुत्र (जहाँ माजुली द्वीप है) तथा बांग्लादेश में जमुना कहलाती है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Right-bank tributaries of Brahmaputra: Subansiri, Kameng, Manas, Sankosh, Teesta. (2) Left-bank tributaries: Dibang, Lohit, Dhansiri, Kopili. (3) After Jamuna (Brahmaputra) meets Padma (Ganga) and Meghna in Bangladesh, they form the Sundarbans Delta. (4) National Waterway-2 (NW-2) runs from Sadiya to Dhubri on the Brahmaputra (891 km).
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding the Brahmaputra River:
Statement I: In Tibet, the Brahmaputra is known as Yarlung Tsangpo and enters India through Arunachal Pradesh as the Dihang/Siang.
Statement II: Majuli, the world's largest inhabited river island, is formed by the Brahmaputra in Assam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II

q:
पूर्व की ओर बहने वाली निम्नलिखित प्रायद्वीपीय नदियों को उत्तर से दक्षिण के क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
1. कृष्णा  2. महानदी  3. कावेरी  4. गोदावरी
e:
Moving North to South along India's eastern coast: Mahanadi (Odisha) → Godavari (AP) → Krishna (AP) → Pennar → Kaveri (Tamil Nadu) → Vaigai. Thus the correct order is 2, 4, 1, 3.
हिंदी: उत्तर से दक्षिण क्रम: महानदी (2) → गोदावरी (4) → कृष्णा (1) → कावेरी (3)।
Exam Boosters: (1) Subarnarekha and Baitarani/Brahmani lie just north of Mahanadi. (2) Kaveri forms the Shivasamudram waterfall and Srirangapatna river island in Karnataka. (3) The Krishna-Godavari (KG) Basin is famous for offshore natural gas reserves. (4) West-flowing rivers like Narmada, Tapti, Mandovi, Zuari, and Periyar form estuaries rather than deltas.
qe:
Arrange the following east-flowing Peninsular rivers from North to South:
1. Krishna  2. Mahanadi  3. Kaveri  4. Godavari

q: उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत (पंजाब, हरियाणा, पश्चिमी यूपी) में शीतकालीन वर्षा, जो गेहूँ जैसी रबी फसलों के लिए लाभदायक होती है, किसके कारण होती है?
o: बंगाल की खाड़ी के उष्णकटिबंधीय चक्रवात
e:
Western Disturbances are extra-tropical cyclonic storms originating over the Mediterranean Sea and brought to North-West India by the Subtropical Westerly Jet Stream during winter.
हिंदी: पश्चिमी विक्षोभ भूमध्य सागर से उत्पन्न होने वाले शीतोष्ण चक्रवात हैं जो पश्चिमी जेट स्ट्रीम द्वारा भारत में लाए जाते हैं और शीतकालीन वर्षा (मावठ) करते हैं।
Exam Boosters: (1) In Rajasthan, this winter rainfall is locally called 'Mahawat'. (2) Tamil Nadu (Coromandel Coast) receives winter rainfall from the North-East (retreating) Monsoon, NOT Western Disturbances. (3) Pre-monsoon showers: 'Mango Showers' (Kerala/Karnataka), 'Blossom Showers' (coffee in Kerala), 'Nor'westers / Kal Baisakhi' (West Bengal/Assam). (4) Mawsynram (Meghalaya, Khasi Hills) receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world.
qe: Winter rainfall in North-Western India (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP) that benefits Rabi crops like wheat is caused by:
oe: Tropical Cyclones of Bay of Bengal

q: भारत की किस मृदा को स्थानीय रूप से 'रेगुर' कहा जाता है तथा जो उच्च नमी धारण क्षमता के कारण कपास की खेती के लिए सर्वोत्तम है?
e:
Black Soil (Regur / Tropical Chernozem) develops from weathering of Deccan basaltic lava, covers Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP, and parts of AP/Karnataka, and develops deep cracks when dry ('self-ploughing' soil).
हिंदी: काली मृदा (रेगुर) दक्कन के बेसाल्ट लावा के अपक्षय से बनती है; सूखने पर इसमें दरारें पड़ने से इसे 'स्वतः जुताई वाली मृदा' भी कहा जाता है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Alluvial Soil covers the largest area in India (~43%), rich in potash but poor in nitrogen and phosphorus. (2) Red Soil gets its red colour from ferric oxide (iron) in crystalline igneous rocks. (3) Laterite Soil forms under high temperature and heavy rainfall by intense leaching; suitable for cashew, tea, coffee, and brick-making. (4) Peaty/Marshy soils are rich in organic matter (humus) and found in Kerala (Kari) and Sundarbans.
qe: Which soil type of India is locally known as 'Regur' and is ideal for cotton cultivation due to its high moisture-retaining capacity?

q: भारत के सर्वाधिक भौगोलिक क्षेत्रफल पर किस प्रकार की प्राकृतिक वनस्पति पाई जाती है?
e:
Tropical Deciduous Forests (also called Monsoon Forests, receiving 70–200 cm annual rainfall) are the most widespread forest type in India, subdivided into Moist Deciduous (Teak, Sal, Sandalwood) and Dry Deciduous.
हिंदी: उष्णकटिबंधीय पर्णपाती वन (मानसूनी वन, 70–200 सेमी वर्षा) भारत में सर्वाधिक क्षेत्रफल पर फैले हैं, जिनमें सागौन, साल, शीशम व चंदन प्रमुख वृक्ष हैं।
Exam Boosters: (1) Tropical Evergreen Forests (>200 cm rainfall) occur in Western Ghats, Andaman & Nicobar, and Northeast India (Mahogany, Ebony, Rosewood). (2) Sundarbans (West Bengal) is the largest mangrove forest in the world, named after the 'Sundari' tree. (3) According to India State of Forest Report (ISFR), Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover by area, while Mizoram has the highest percentage forest cover. (4) Project Tiger was launched in 1973 from Jim Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand).
qe: Which type of natural vegetation covers the largest geographical area in India?

q:
सूची-I (जैवमंडल आरक्षित क्षेत्र) को सूची-II (राज्य) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
सूची-I: (a) नोकरेक  (b) सिमलीपाल  (c) पचमढ़ी  (d) अगस्त्यमलाई
सूची-II: 1. ओडिशा  2. मेघालय  3. केरल-तमिलनाडु  4. मध्य प्रदेश
e:
Nokrek is in Meghalaya (2); Similipal is in Odisha (1); Pachmarhi is in Madhya Pradesh (4); Agasthyamalai spans Kerala and Tamil Nadu (3). Code: a-2, b-1, c-4, d-3.
हिंदी: नोकरेक (मेघालय), सिमलीपाल (ओडिशा), पचमढ़ी (मध्य प्रदेश) तथा अगस्त्यमलाई (केरल-तमिलनाडु) सही युग्म हैं। कूट: a-2, b-1, c-4, d-3।
Exam Boosters: (1) India has 18 Biosphere Reserves, of which 12 are part of UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves (MAB Programme). (2) Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (1986, TN–Kerala–Karnataka) was India's first Biosphere Reserve. (3) Panna (MP) was the 12th Indian reserve added to UNESCO's MAB network. (4) Kachchh (Gujarat) is the largest Biosphere Reserve in India by area, while Dibru-Saikhowa (Assam) is the smallest.
qe:
Match List-I (Biosphere Reserves) with List-II (States):
List-I: (a) Nokrek  (b) Similipal  (c) Pachmarhi  (d) Agasthyamalai
List-II: 1. Odisha  2. Meghalaya  3. Kerala–Tamil Nadu  4. Madhya Pradesh

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा राष्ट्रीय उद्यान अपने राज्य से सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
e:
Silent Valley National Park is located in the Nilgiri Hills of Palakkad district in KERALA (famous for the endangered Lion-tailed Macaque), NOT Karnataka.
हिंदी: साइलेंट वैली राष्ट्रीय उद्यान केरल (पलक्कड़ जिला) में स्थित है, न कि कर्नाटक में। यह सिंह-पुच्छ मकाक के लिए प्रसिद्ध है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Kaziranga (Assam) is famous for the One-horned Rhinoceros; Manas is also in Assam. (2) Dachigam (J&K) protects the Kashmiri Stag (Hangul). (3) Gir National Park (Gujarat) is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion. (4) Bandipur, Nagarhole, and Bannerghatta are prominent National Parks in Karnataka; Dudhwa is the only National Park in Uttar Pradesh.
qe: Which of the following National Parks is NOT correctly matched with its state?

q: प्रशांत महासागर में एक प्रबल 'अल-नीनो' (El Niño) घटना सामान्यतः भारतीय दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून को कैसे प्रभावित करती है?
o: सामान्य से अधिक वर्षा और बाढ़ लाती है
मानसून को कमजोर करती है, जिससे प्रायः सूखा पड़ता है
मई में मानसून का शीघ्र आगमन कराती है
भारतीय मानसून वर्षा पर कोई प्रभाव नहीं डालती
e:
El Niño refers to abnormal warming of eastern/central equatorial Pacific waters (off Peru), which weakens the Walker Circulation and Pacific trade winds, suppressing monsoon rainfall over India and increasing drought risk.
हिंदी: अल-नीनो पूर्वी प्रशांत महासागर के जल के असामान्य रूप से गर्म होने की घटना है, जो भारतीय मानसून को कमजोर कर सूखे की स्थिति उत्पन्न करती है।
Exam Boosters: (1) La Niña (abnormal cooling of eastern Pacific) generally strengthens the Indian Monsoon and brings abundant rainfall. (2) Positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) — warmer western Indian Ocean than eastern — counteracts El Niño and boosts Indian monsoon rains. (3) The onset of SW Monsoon hits Kerala coast around 1 June. (4) ITCZ (Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone) shifts northward over the Ganga plain in summer, creating a low-pressure monsoon trough.
qe: How does a strong 'El Niño' event in the Pacific Ocean typically affect the Indian South-West Monsoon?
oe: Weakens the monsoon, often causing drought
Triggers early onset of monsoon in May
Has no effect on Indian monsoon rainfall

q: भारत में लैटेराइट मृदा (Laterite Soil) के निर्माण के लिए मुख्य रूप से कौन-सी प्रक्रिया उत्तरदायी है?
o: भारी वर्षा व उच्च तापमान के कारण तीव्र निक्षालन
e:
Laterite soil forms in regions of high temperature and heavy rainfall (Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, Meghalaya, Odisha) through intense leaching, where silica and lime wash away leaving iron and aluminium oxides behind.
हिंदी: उच्च तापमान और भारी वर्षा वाले क्षेत्रों में तीव्र निक्षालन (leaching) से सिलिका व चूना बह जाता है तथा लौह व एल्युमिनियम ऑक्साइड शेष रहकर लैटेराइट मृदा बनाते हैं।
Exam Boosters: (1) The word 'Laterite' comes from Latin 'later' meaning brick — it hardens like brick upon drying. (2) Laterite soil is poor in nitrogen, potash, and humus, but supports plantation crops like cashew, tea, coffee, and rubber. (3) ICAR classifies Indian soils into 8 major groups. (4) Saline/Alkaline soils are locally known as Reh, Usar, or Kallar in UP and Punjab; Gypsum is used to reclaim alkaline soils.
qe: Which process is primarily responsible for the formation of Laterite Soil in India?
oe: Intense leaching due to heavy rain and high temperature

q: भारत के किस राज्य में रामसर आर्द्रभूमि (Ramsar Wetland) स्थलों की संख्या सर्वाधिक है?
e:
Tamil Nadu has the largest number of Ramsar wetland sites in India (followed by Uttar Pradesh in second place).
हिंदी: भारत में सर्वाधिक रामसर आर्द्रभूमि स्थल तमिलनाडु राज्य में स्थित हैं, जबकि उत्तर प्रदेश दूसरे स्थान पर है।
Exam Boosters: (1) The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was signed on 2 February 1971 in Ramsar, Iran; World Wetlands Day is celebrated on 2 February. (2) UP has 10 Ramsar sites including Upper Ganga River, Nawabganj, Saman, Samaspur, Sandi, Sarsai Nawar, Parvati Arga, Sur Sarovar, Haiderpur, and Bakhira. (3) Renuka Wetland (Himachal Pradesh) is India's smallest Ramsar site; Sundarbans (West Bengal) is the largest. (4) Montreux Record is a register of Ramsar sites facing ecological change (in India: Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake).
qe: Which Indian state has the highest number of Ramsar wetland sites?

q:
भारतीय मानसून के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून की अरब सागर शाखा, बंगाल की खाड़ी शाखा की तुलना में अधिक प्रबल होती है।
कथन II: दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून के दौरान तमिलनाडु में बहुत कम वर्षा होती है क्योंकि यह पश्चिमी घाट के वृष्टि-छाया क्षेत्र में तथा बंगाल की खाड़ी शाखा के समांतर स्थित है।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: कथन I और कथन II दोनों
न तो कथन I और न ही कथन II
e:
Both statements are correct. The Arabian Sea branch is larger/stronger (~65% of monsoon moisture) than the Bay of Bengal branch (~35%). Tamil Nadu stays dry in summer because it lies on the leeward (rain-shadow) side of the Western Ghats and parallel to the Bay of Bengal winds.
हिंदी: दोनों कथन सत्य हैं। अरब सागर शाखा अधिक प्रबल है, और तमिलनाडु पश्चिमी घाट के वृष्टि-छाया क्षेत्र व बंगाल की खाड़ी शाखा के समांतर होने के कारण ग्रीष्म मानसून में शुष्क रहता है।
Exam Boosters: (1) October Heat occurs during the retreating monsoon due to high temperature and high humidity after clear skies return. (2) Aravalli Range runs parallel to the Arabian Sea branch, causing scanty rainfall in Western Rajasthan (Thar Desert). (3) The rain-shadow zone of the Western Ghats includes interior Maharashtra (Vidarbha/Marathwada), Rayalaseema, and interior Karnataka. (4) According to Köppen's climatic classification, most of the Ganga plain falls under 'Cwg' (monsoon with dry winter).
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Monsoon:
Statement I: The Arabian Sea branch of the South-West Monsoon is stronger and carries more moisture than the Bay of Bengal branch.
Statement II: Tamil Nadu receives very little rainfall during the South-West Monsoon because it lies in the rain-shadow region of the Western Ghats and runs parallel to the Bay of Bengal branch.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II

q:
पूर्वी हिमालय में निम्नलिखित वनस्पति कटिबंधों को कम ऊँचाई से अधिक ऊँचाई के क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
1. अल्पाइन घास के मैदान  2. उष्णकटिबंधीय आर्द्र सदाबहार  3. शीतोष्ण चौड़ी पत्ती/शंकुधारी  4. उपोष्णकटिबंधीय चीड़/चौड़ी पत्ती
e:
Moving upward in altitude in the Eastern Himalayas: Tropical wet evergreen (foothills up to ~1000 m) → Sub-tropical (1000–2000 m) → Temperate broad-leaved & coniferous (2000–3500 m) → Alpine meadows/Tundra (>3500 m). Order: 2, 4, 3, 1.
हिंदी: कम से अधिक ऊँचाई का क्रम: उष्णकटिबंधीय सदाबहार (2) → उपोष्णकटिबंधीय (4) → शीतोष्ण शंकुधारी (3) → अल्पाइन घास के मैदान (1)।
Exam Boosters: (1) Alpine meadows are called 'Bugyals' in Uttarakhand and 'Margs' (e.g., Gulmarg, Sonamarg) in Jammu & Kashmir. (2) Snow line is lower in the Western Himalayas than in the Eastern Himalayas due to higher latitude and lower precipitation. (3) Shola forests are temperate montane forests found in the Nilgiri, Anaimalai, and Palani hills of South India. (4) Deodar, Chir Pine, Silver Fir, and Juniper are key Himalayan conifers.
qe:
In the Eastern Himalayas, arrange the following vegetation zones from lower altitude to higher altitude:
1. Alpine meadows  2. Tropical wet evergreen  3. Temperate broad-leaved/coniferous  4. Sub-tropical pine/broad-leaved

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी एक रबी फसल है जो भारत में अक्टूबर–दिसंबर में बोई जाती है तथा अप्रैल–जून में काटी जाती है?
e:
Mustard (along with wheat, barley, gram, and peas) is a classic Rabi (winter) crop. Paddy, cotton, groundnut, maize, jowar, and bajra are Kharif (monsoon) crops.
हिंदी: सरसों (गेहूँ, जौ, चना, मटर के साथ) रबी की प्रमुख फसल है, जबकि धान, कपास और मूँगफली खरीफ की फसलें हैं।
Exam Boosters: (1) Zaid crops (March–June, between Rabi and Kharif) include watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, and fodder crops. (2) Leading producing states: Uttar Pradesh (Wheat, Sugarcane, Potato), West Bengal (Rice, Jute), Rajasthan (Mustard, Bajra), Madhya Pradesh (Soyabean, Pulses), Gujarat (Groundnut, Cotton). (3) Green Revolution (1966-67) had maximum impact on Wheat and Rice in Punjab, Haryana, and Western UP; M.S. Swaminathan is its father in India. (4) 'Operation Flood' (White Revolution, 1970) was led by Dr. Verghese Kurien.
qe: Which of the following is strictly a Rabi crop sown in October–December and harvested in April–June in India?

q: राजस्थान की खेतड़ी खानें भारत में किस खनिज के उत्पादन के लिए प्रसिद्ध हैं?
e:
The Khetri-Singhana belt in Jhunjhunu district (Rajasthan) is India's most famous historic copper-mining region, operated by Hindustan Copper Limited.
हिंदी: राजस्थान के झुंझुनू जिले की खेतड़ी-सिंघाना पट्टी भारत में ताँबा (Copper) उत्पादन के लिए प्रसिद्ध है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Malanjkhand (Balaghat, MP) is India's largest open-cast copper mine; Singhbhum (Jharkhand) is another major copper belt. (2) Odisha is India's leading producer of Iron Ore, Bauxite, Chromite, and Manganese. (3) Kudremukh and Bellary (Karnataka), Bailadila (Chhattisgarh), and Mayurbhanj/Keonjhar (Odisha) are famous iron ore belts. (4) Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh belt (Jharkhand–Bihar) and Nellore (AP) are renowned for Mica.
qe: Which mineral belt of India is famous for the Khetri mines in Rajasthan?

q: उत्तर में श्रीनगर को दक्षिण में कन्याकुमारी से जोड़ने वाला भारत का सबसे लंबा राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग कौन-सा है?
e:
National Highway 44 (NH 44, ~3,745 km) is India's longest National Highway, running from Srinagar (J&K) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu), forming the North-South Corridor.
हिंदी: राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 44 (NH 44) श्रीनगर से कन्याकुमारी तक भारत का सबसे लंबा राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग है।
Exam Boosters: (1) NH 27 forms the East-West Corridor (Porbandar, Gujarat to Silchar, Assam); the North-South and East-West Corridors intersect at Jhansi (UP). (2) Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata (5,846 km). (3) National Waterway-1 (NW-1, 1,620 km) runs from Prayagraj to Haldia on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system. (4) NH 19 is the historic Grand Trunk Road section connecting Delhi to Kolkata.
qe: Which is the longest National Highway in India, connecting Srinagar in the north to Kanyakumari in the south?

q:
सूची-I (परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र) को सूची-II (राज्य) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
सूची-I: (a) नरोरा  (b) काकरापार  (c) कैगा  (d) कुडनकुलम
सूची-II: 1. गुजरात  2. तमिलनाडु  3. उत्तर प्रदेश  4. कर्नाटक
e:
Narora is in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh (3); Kakrapar is in Gujarat (1); Kaiga is in Karnataka (4); Kudankulam (largest nuclear power station in India, built with Russian collaboration) is in Tamil Nadu (2).
हिंदी: नरोरा (उत्तर प्रदेश), काकरापार (गुजरात), कैगा (कर्नाटक) तथा कुडनकुलम (तमिलनाडु) सही सुमेलित हैं। कूट: a-3, b-1, c-4, d-2।
Exam Boosters: (1) Tarapur (Maharashtra, 1969) is India's oldest commercial nuclear power station. (2) Rawatbhata (Rajasthan) and Kalpakkam (Tamil Nadu) are the other operational nuclear plants. (3) Jaduguda (Singhbhum, Jharkhand) is India's first and most famous Uranium mine; Monazite sands of Kerala are rich in Thorium. (4) India's first nuclear research reactor was 'Apsara' (Trombay, 1956).
qe:
Match List-I (Nuclear Power Plants) with List-II (States):
List-I: (a) Narora  (b) Kakrapar  (c) Kaiga  (d) Kudankulam
List-II: 1. Gujarat  2. Tamil Nadu  3. Uttar Pradesh  4. Karnataka

q: भारत का निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा प्रमुख बंदरगाह कच्छ की खाड़ी में स्थित एक ज्वारीय बंदरगाह (tidal port) है?
e:
Deendayal Port (formerly Kandla Port) in Gujarat is a major tidal port developed after Partition to ease pressure on Mumbai Port and serve northern/western India.
हिंदी: गुजरात में कच्छ की खाड़ी पर स्थित दीनदयाल (कांडला) बंदरगाह एक प्रमुख ज्वारीय बंदरगाह है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) is India's deepest landlocked natural port. (2) Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva, Maharashtra) is India's largest container port. (3) Kolkata–Haldia (Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port) is India's only major riverine port (on Hooghly river). (4) Mormugao (Goa) is a key iron-ore exporting port; Kochi (Kerala) is called the 'Queen of the Arabian Sea'.
qe: Which of the following Major Ports of India is a tidal port located on the Gulf of Kachchh?

q: झारखंड का कौन-सा कोयला क्षेत्र भारत में उच्च कोटि के कोकिंग कोयले (prime coking coal) का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक है?
e:
Jharia Coalfield (Dhanbad, Jharkhand) is the single largest source of prime coking coal in India, essential for the iron and steel industry.
हिंदी: झारखंड के धनबाद जिले में स्थित झरिया कोयला क्षेत्र भारत में उच्च कोटि के कोकिंग कोयले का सबसे बड़ा भंडार एवं उत्पादक है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Raniganj (West Bengal) is the oldest coalfield in India (mining began in 1774). (2) Over 98% of India's coal reserves belong to the Gondwana age (Damodar, Son, Mahanadi, Godavari valleys). (3) Neyveli (Tamil Nadu) is India's largest Lignite (brown coal) deposit. (4) Singrauli (MP–UP border, Sonbhadra) is known as the 'Energy Capital of India'; Korba is in Chhattisgarh and Talcher is in Odisha.
qe: Which coalfield in Jharkhand is the largest producer of prime coking coal in India?

q: उत्तर मध्य रेलवे (North Central Railway) ज़ोन का मुख्यालय कहाँ स्थित है?
e:
North Central Railway (NCR) is headquartered at Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh), while North Eastern Railway (NER) is headquartered at Gorakhpur (UP).
हिंदी: उत्तर मध्य रेलवे (NCR) का मुख्यालय प्रयागराज में स्थित है, जबकि पूर्वोत्तर रेलवे (NER) का मुख्यालय गोरखपुर में है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Indian Railways is organized into 18 operational zones (plus Metro Railway Kolkata; South Coast Railway at Visakhapatnam is the newest zone). (2) Northern Railway HQ: New Delhi; Eastern Railway & South Eastern Railway HQ: Kolkata; Central & Western Railway HQ: Mumbai. (3) India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 between Bori Bunder (Mumbai) and Thane (34 km). (4) Konkan Railway connects Roha (Maharashtra) to Thokur/Mangaluru (Karnataka) along the Western Ghats.
qe: Where is the headquarters of the North Central Railway (NCR) zone located?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी कृषि क्रांति अपने प्रमुख उत्पाद से सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
o: रजत क्रांति — अंडा एवं कुक्कुट उत्पादन
e:
Golden Revolution relates to Horticulture, Fruits, and Honey production (father: Nirpakh Tutej), whereas Jute production is associated with the Golden Fibre Revolution.
हिंदी: स्वर्ण क्रांति (Golden Revolution) बागवानी, फल व शहद उत्पादन से संबंधित है, जबकि जूट उत्पादन 'स्वर्ण रेशा क्रांति' (Golden Fibre Revolution) से जुड़ा है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Silver Fibre Revolution → Cotton; Grey Revolution → Fertilizers; Pink Revolution → Onion/Prawn/Pharmaceuticals; Round Revolution → Potato. (2) Black Revolution → Petroleum/Crude oil; Brown Revolution → Leather/Cocoa/Non-conventional energy. (3) India is the world's largest producer of Milk, Pulses, Jute, and Spices, and 2nd largest in Rice, Wheat, Sugarcane, and Cotton. (4) Minimum Support Price (MSP) is recommended by CACP (Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices) and approved by CCEA.
qe: Which of the following agricultural revolutions is NOT correctly matched with its primary product?

q:
द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना के दौरान स्थापित भारत के लौह-इस्पात संयंत्रों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: भिलाई इस्पात संयंत्र (छत्तीसगढ़) की स्थापना सोवियत संघ (रूस) के सहयोग से हुई थी।
कथन II: राउरकेला इस्पात संयंत्र (ओडिशा) की स्थापना यूनाइटेड किंगडम (ब्रिटेन) के सहयोग से हुई थी।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: कथन I और कथन II दोनों
न तो कथन I और न ही कथन II
e:
Statement I is correct (Bhilai — USSR). Statement II is incorrect because Rourkela Steel Plant (Odisha) was built with assistance from West Germany (Krupp & Demag), whereas Durgapur Steel Plant (West Bengal) was built with UK assistance.
हिंदी: कथन I सही है। कथन II गलत है क्योंकि राउरकेला इस्पात संयंत्र (ओडिशा) पश्चिमी जर्मनी के सहयोग से स्थापित हुआ था, जबकि दुर्गापुर (पश्चिम बंगाल) ब्रिटेन के सहयोग से बना।
Exam Boosters: (1) Bokaro Steel Plant (Jharkhand, 3rd Five-Year Plan) was also established with USSR collaboration. (2) TISCO (Tata Iron and Steel Company, Jamshedpur, 1907) was India's first modern integrated private steel plant (at confluence of Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers). (3) Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (RINL) is India's first shore-based integrated steel plant. (4) Salem (Tamil Nadu) is famous for stainless steel; Vijayanagar (Karnataka) uses Bellary iron ore.
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding India's Iron and Steel plants set up during the Second Five-Year Plan:
Statement I: Bhilai Steel Plant (Chhattisgarh) was established with assistance from the USSR (Russia).
Statement II: Rourkela Steel Plant (Odisha) was established with assistance from the United Kingdom.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II

q: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार वर्ष 2001–2011 के दौरान भारत की दशकीय जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर क्या थी?
e:
India's population grew from 102.87 crore (2001) to 121.09 crore (2011), recording a decadal growth rate of 17.70% (down from 21.54% in 1991–2001).
हिंदी: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार 2001–2011 के मध्य भारत की दशकीय जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर 17.70% रही (जो 1991–2001 के 21.54% से कम थी)।
Exam Boosters: (1) Among states, Meghalaya recorded the highest decadal growth rate (+27.9%), while Nagaland was the ONLY state with negative growth (−0.6%). (2) Among UTs, Dadra & Nagar Haveli had the highest decadal growth (+55.9%). (3) Uttar Pradesh's decadal growth rate was 20.23% (population 19.98 crore, ~16.5% of India's total). (4) Census 2011 was the 15th Census of India overall and the 7th after Independence (Motto: 'Our Census, Our Future').
qe: According to Census 2011, what was the decadal population growth rate of India during 2001–2011?

q: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार भारत का कुल लिंगानुपात (प्रति 1,000 पुरुषों पर महिलाएँ) कितना था?
e:
India's overall Sex Ratio improved from 933 in 2001 to 943 females per 1,000 males in Census 2011.
हिंदी: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार भारत का कुल लिंगानुपात 943 (प्रति 1,000 पुरुषों पर महिलाएँ) था, जो 2001 के 933 से 10 अंक अधिक था।
Exam Boosters: (1) Highest Sex Ratio among states: Kerala (1,084), followed by Tamil Nadu (996) and Andhra Pradesh (993). (2) Lowest Sex Ratio among states: Haryana (879), followed by J&K (889) and Sikkim (890). (3) India's Child Sex Ratio (0–6 years) fell to 919 in 2011 (highest: Arunachal Pradesh 972; lowest: Haryana 834). (4) Uttar Pradesh's overall Sex Ratio in 2011 was 912 (Child Sex Ratio: 902).
qe: According to Census 2011, what was the overall Sex Ratio (females per 1,000 males) of India?

q: भारत के जनसांख्यिकीय इतिहास में किस वर्ष को 'महाविभाजक वर्ष' (Year of Great Divide) कहा जाता है?
e:
1921 is called the 'Year of Great Divide' because 1911–1921 was the ONLY census decade in Indian history to record a negative population growth rate (−0.31%) due to famines and the 1918 influenza pandemic; after 1921, India's population grew continuously.
हिंदी: 1911–1921 का दशक भारतीय जनगणना इतिहास का एकमात्र दशक था जिसमें जनसंख्या वृद्धि ऋणात्मक (−0.31%) रही। 1921 के बाद जनसंख्या में निरंतर वृद्धि हुई, अतः 1921 को महाविभाजक वर्ष कहा जाता है।
Exam Boosters: (1) 1951 is called the 'Year of Small Divide' (start of rapid population explosion phase: 1951–1981). (2) First non-synchronous census in India was held in 1872 (under Lord Mayo); first synchronous regular decennial census began in 1881 (under Lord Ripon). (3) The highest ever decadal growth rate in India was 24.80% during 1961–1971. (4) Four stages of India's demographic history: 1901–21 (Stagnant), 1921–51 (Steady growth), 1951–81 (Population explosion), 1981–present (High growth with definite signs of slowing down).
qe: Which year is known as the 'Year of Great Divide' in the demographic history of India?

q: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार भारत की प्रभावी साक्षरता दर (7 वर्ष और उससे अधिक आयु के लिए) क्या थी?
e:
As per the final Census 2011 figures (PCA), India's overall literacy rate was 73.00% (provisional was 74.04%), with Male literacy at 80.9% and Female literacy at 64.6%. (Note: In UPPSC/UPESSC exams where both 73.00% and 74.04% appear, 73.00% is the final official Census 2011 figure.)
हिंदी: जनगणना 2011 के अंतिम आँकड़ों के अनुसार भारत की कुल साक्षरता दर 73.00% थी (पुरुष: 80.9%, महिला: 64.6%)। (अनंतिम आँकड़ा 74.04% था।)
Exam Boosters: (1) Highest Literacy states: Kerala (94.0%), Mizoram (91.3%), Goa (88.7%); highest UT: Lakshadweep (91.8%). (2) Lowest Literacy states: Bihar (61.8%), Arunachal Pradesh (65.4%), Rajasthan (66.1%). (3) Rajasthan recorded the highest male-female literacy gap, while Meghalaya had the lowest gap. (4) Uttar Pradesh's literacy rate in 2011 was 67.7% (Male: 77.3%, Female: 57.2%).
qe: According to Census 2011, what was the effective Literacy Rate of India (for population aged 7 years and above)?

q: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार भारत का जनसंख्या घनत्व (व्यक्ति प्रति वर्ग किमी) कितना था?
e:
India's population density increased by 57 persons/sq km from 325 in 2001 to 382 persons per sq. km in Census 2011.
हिंदी: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार भारत का जनसंख्या घनत्व 382 व्यक्ति प्रति वर्ग किमी था (2001 में यह 325 था)।
Exam Boosters: (1) Highest density states: Bihar (1,106) > West Bengal (1,028) > Kerala (860) > Uttar Pradesh (829). (2) Lowest density states: Arunachal Pradesh (17) < Mizoram (52) < Sikkim (86). (3) Highest density UT: NCT of Delhi (11,320/sq km); lowest density UT: Andaman & Nicobar Islands (46/sq km). (4) In UP, Ghaziabad has the highest density (3,971/sq km) and Lalitpur the lowest (242/sq km).
qe: According to Census 2011, what was the population density of India (persons per sq. km)?

q: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार भारत की कुल जनसंख्या का कितना प्रतिशत भाग नगरीय क्षेत्रों में निवास करता था?
e:
In Census 2011, 31.16% of India's population (37.71 crore) was urban and 68.84% (83.37 crore) was rural (up from 27.81% urban in 2001).
हिंदी: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार भारत की 31.16% जनसंख्या नगरीय और 68.84% जनसंख्या ग्रामीण थी।
Exam Boosters: (1) Most urbanized state by percentage: Goa (62.2%), followed by Mizoram (52.1%) and Tamil Nadu (48.4%). (2) Least urbanized state by percentage: Himachal Pradesh (10.0%), followed by Bihar (11.3%). (3) Largest urban population in absolute numbers: Maharashtra (5.08 crore), followed by Uttar Pradesh (4.45 crore; UP's urbanization is 22.27%). (4) Census 2011 recorded 53 Million-Plus urban agglomerations/cities in India (up from 35 in 2001).
qe: According to Census 2011, what percentage of India's total population lived in urban areas?

q: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार किस भारतीय राज्य में अनुसूचित जनजाति (ST) की जनसंख्या संख्यात्मक दृष्टि से सर्वाधिक है?
e:
Madhya Pradesh has the largest Scheduled Tribe population in absolute numbers (~1.53 crore, 14.7% of India's total ST population), followed by Maharashtra and Odisha.
हिंदी: संख्या की दृष्टि से सर्वाधिक अनुसूचित जनजाति (ST) जनसंख्या मध्य प्रदेश में निवास करती है (भारत की कुल ST जनसंख्या का 14.7%)।
Exam Boosters: (1) Highest ST percentage among states: Mizoram (94.4%), followed by Nagaland (86.5%); highest among UTs: Lakshadweep (94.8%). (2) States/UTs with ZERO notified ST population in Census 2011: Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, and Puducherry. (3) Total ST share in India's population is 8.6% (SC share is 16.6%). (4) Bhil is the largest tribal group in India, followed by Gond and Santhal; Tharu is the largest tribe in Uttar Pradesh.
qe: According to Census 2011, which Indian state has the highest Scheduled Tribe (ST) population in absolute numbers?

q:
सूची-I (जनजातीय समूह) को सूची-II (प्रमुख राज्य/केंद्र शासित प्रदेश) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
सूची-I: (a) टोडा  (b) जारवा  (c) भूटिया  (d) अपातानी
सूची-II: 1. अरुणाचल प्रदेश  2. सिक्किम  3. तमिलनाडु  4. अंडमान एवं निकोबार द्वीप समूह
e:
Toda (pastoral tribe of Nilgiri Hills) — Tamil Nadu (3); Jarawa (PVTG) — Andaman & Nicobar Islands (4); Bhutia (along with Lepcha) — Sikkim (2); Apatani — Arunachal Pradesh (1). Code: a-3, b-4, c-2, d-1.
हिंदी: टोडा (तमिलनाडु/नीलगिरि), जारवा (अंडमान-निकोबार), भूटिया (सिक्किम) तथा अपातानी (अरुणाचल प्रदेश) सही सुमेलित हैं। कूट: a-3, b-4, c-2, d-1।
Exam Boosters: (1) Onge, Sentinelese, Great Andamanese, and Shompen are other PVTGs of Andaman & Nicobar Islands. (2) India has 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), with Odisha having the highest number (13). (3) Gaddi and Gujjar are transhumant pastoral tribes of Himachal Pradesh and J&K; Changpa live in Ladakh. (4) Chenchu live in Andhra Pradesh/Telangana; Garo, Khasi, Jaintia in Meghalaya.
qe:
Match List-I (Tribal Groups) with List-II (Primary States/UTs):
List-I: (a) Toda  (b) Jarawa  (c) Bhutia  (d) Apatani
List-II: 1. Arunachal Pradesh  2. Sikkim  3. Tamil Nadu  4. Andaman & Nicobar Islands

q: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार भारत में अनुसूचित जाति (SC) जनसंख्या के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
o: उत्तर प्रदेश में संख्यात्मक दृष्टि से सर्वाधिक SC जनसंख्या है
सभी राज्यों में SC जनसंख्या का सर्वाधिक प्रतिशत पंजाब में है
नागालैंड और अरुणाचल प्रदेश में SC जनसंख्या शून्य है
यूपी के बाद भारत में दूसरी सर्वाधिक SC जनसंख्या बिहार में है
e:
Statement D is NOT correct: West Bengal (2.15 crore) has the SECOND largest SC population in India after Uttar Pradesh (4.14 crore), followed by Bihar in third place. Statements A, B (Punjab: 31.9%), and C are correct.
हिंदी: कथन D असत्य है क्योंकि उत्तर प्रदेश के बाद भारत में दूसरी सर्वाधिक अनुसूचित जाति (SC) जनसंख्या पश्चिम बंगाल में है (बिहार तीसरे स्थान पर है)।
Exam Boosters: (1) Punjab (31.9%), Himachal Pradesh (25.2%), and West Bengal (23.5%) lead in SC percentage share. (2) States/UTs with ZERO SC population in 2011: Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, Lakshadweep, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands. (3) Total SC population in India (2011) was 20.14 crore (16.6% of total population). (4) In UP, Sitapur has the highest SC population in numbers, while Kaushambi has the highest SC percentage.
qe: According to Census 2011, which of the following statements regarding Scheduled Castes (SC) in India is NOT correct?
oe: Uttar Pradesh has the largest SC population in absolute numbers
Punjab has the highest percentage of SC population among all states
Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh have zero SC population
Bihar has the second largest SC population in India after UP

q:
जनगणना 2011 की 'जनगणना नगर' (Census Town) परिभाषा तथा भारतीय प्रवासन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: किसी बस्ती को 'जनगणना नगर' तभी माना जाता है जब उसकी न्यूनतम जनसंख्या 5,000 हो, कम से कम 75% पुरुष मुख्य कार्यशील जनसंख्या गैर-कृषि कार्यों में संलग्न हो तथा जनसंख्या घनत्व कम से कम 400 व्यक्ति प्रति वर्ग किमी हो।
कथन II: भारत में आंतरिक प्रवासन की सबसे बड़ी धारा ग्रामीण-से-ग्रामीण है, जिसमें विवाह के कारण महिला प्रवासन प्रमुख है।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: कथन I और कथन II दोनों
न तो कथन I और न ही कथन II
e:
Both statements are completely accurate. Census 2011 defines a Census Town using the exact three criteria in Statement I (5,000 population, 75% male non-agricultural main workers, 400/sq km density). In internal migration, Rural-to-Rural accounts for the largest share (~47%), predominantly women migrating after marriage, while Rural-to-Urban is dominated by male work/employment migration.
हिंदी: दोनों कथन पूर्णतः सत्य हैं। जनगणना नगर के तीनों मानक (5,000 जनसंख्या, 75% गैर-कृषि पुरुष मुख्य श्रमिक, 400 घनत्व) सही हैं, तथा भारत में सर्वाधिक आंतरिक प्रवासन ग्रामीण-से-ग्रामीण (मुख्यतः विवाह के कारण महिलाओं का) होता है।
Exam Boosters: (1) Statutory Towns are places with a municipality, corporation, cantonment board, or notified town area committee regardless of demographic criteria. (2) Class I cities have a population of 1,00,000 or more; Million-Plus cities have 10 lakh or more; Mega Cities have 1 crore (10 million) or more (Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata in 2011). (3) UP and Bihar are the largest net out-migration states, while Maharashtra and Delhi are the largest net in-migration destinations. (4) India's Total Fertility Rate (TFR) has declined to 2.0 (NFHS-5), below the replacement level of 2.1.
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding Census 2011 definition of a 'Census Town' and Indian Migration:
Statement I: A settlement qualifies as a 'Census Town' if it has a minimum population of 5,000, at least 75% of its male main working population engaged in non-agricultural pursuits, and a population density of at least 400 persons per sq. km.
Statement II: In India, the largest stream of internal migration is Rural-to-Rural, dominated by female migration due to marriage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II
